speaker: Niles
text: So I just had to get out of the house. Maris' junior league is rehearsing their spring musicale. This year they're doing Cats. For the past week and a half I've been watching two dozen underweight, tightly-pulled women in leotards crawling around the music room, meowing. I'm telling you, Frasier, my allergies are acting up.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, Niles, I think you're exaggerating.

speaker: Niles
text: No, really, you have no idea how vivid the experience is. As God is my judge, I swear Mrs. Presley Bismouth was scent marking the divan.

speaker: Frasier
text: God, you'd think women of that age would choose more suitable material. Remember the last show they did, The Sound of Music? My God, half the Von Trapp children were having hot flashes.

speaker: Roz
text: Hi, Frasier. Niles.

speaker: Niles
text: Let me guess. The wacky gang from the office?

speaker: Frasier
text: Everyone, this is my brother, Niles. This is Teddy, one of our engineers.

speaker: Niles
text: - Teddy, my man. - Niles.

speaker: Frasier
text: This is KACL's own inimitable Chopper Dave. - Your eye in the sky for traffic. - Nice to meet you, Niles.

speaker: Niles
text: - Why is this man yelling? - Oh, was I yelling?

speaker: Dave
text: Oh, God, I was yelling again, wasn't I? I'm sorry. Talking over the blades. You know,

speaker: Niles
text: That's great. This has been kind of fun. Uh... But I really have to go. I'm conducting a seminar in multiple personality disorders, and it takes me forever to fill out the name tags.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, KACL team, what is on the agenda for today?

speaker: Roz
text: Sit down and listen to this. I got a juicy piece of news, and it's reliable. Allen in Accounting got it from Steven in Promotions who got it from Cindy in Sales who got it from Arlene, the station secretary, that the station is definitely way over budget and somebody's getting the ax. But don't tell anybody. I was sworn to secrecy.

speaker: Frasier
text: Roz, I'm ashamed of you. Gossip, gossip, gossip. Don't you realize how destructive it can be? It sullies good people's names, and create an atmosphere of suspicion and mistrust.

speaker: Roz
text: Oh, lighten up! Gossip is the lifeblood of the corporate world. If it wasn't for gossip, we wouldn't know any of the important things. Like how much everybody makes.

speaker: Frasier
text: You know my salary?

speaker: Dave
text: No one's salary's a secret around here.

speaker: Teddy
text: - Ninety-four, 95, 96, 97... - Hey, Bulldog, how's it going?

speaker: Bulldog
text: Great. Ninety-eight, 99, 100. New high for me.

speaker: Roz
text: Squeezing or counting?

speaker: Bulldog
text: Java to go.

speaker: Dave
text: You know who I think's getting dumped? Father Mike from Religion on the Line.

speaker: Roz
text: No way. Station loves him. Just gave him a big bonus.

speaker: Bulldog
text: Hey. Where's my tickets to the Sonics game? They were here just a second ago. Somebody stole my tickets to the Sonics game! This stinks! This is total BS! - This is... - Oh, got them. Got them.

speaker: Roz
text: Hey, you guys don't think it's Bulldog who's getting canned?

speaker: Frasier
text: - Could be. - No, no, no. He's the stations highest-rated personality, with the exception of women between 35 to 54 who think that I'm sort of a god.

speaker: Teddy
text: But he has been in that salary beef with management.

speaker: Roz
text: And I heard him screaming at Business Affairs for putting his expense account on hold.

speaker: Dave
text: Oh, yeah! Bulldog's out!

speaker: unknown
text: Shh!

speaker: Bulldog
text: Hey, have you heard my new gimmick for the show? If the Seahawks beat Buffalo this Sunday, I promise to do my entire show hanging by my feet.

speaker: Frasier
text: Gee, you can do that?

speaker: Bulldog
text: Oh, sure. Practiced all morning. The real trick is drinking coffee. I keep burning my eyes.

speaker: Bulldog
text: Hey, Dave, you want my tickets to the Sonics game tonight?

speaker: Dave
text: Thanks. Why aren't you going?

speaker: Bulldog
text: Station manager wants to see me after work.

speaker: ENSEMBLE
text: Ooh.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, people, people, you're jumping to conclusions. Show a little respect. Bulldog has devoted 15 years of his life to radio. My own personal feelings aside, the man deserves better than to become the object of some rumor that as yet hasn't a shred of truth to it.

speaker: Roz
text: Yeah, I suppose you're right.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yes, well, just in case, I've got dibs on his parking space.

speaker: Roz
text: Dr. Crane, we have Don on his car phone. He's having a problem with his weight.

speaker: unknown
text: Hmm.

speaker: Frasier
text: Don, it's a common problem. I'm listening.

speaker: Don
text: Ah, it's the screwiest thing, doc. I eat healthy. I work out. But no matter what I do, I can't lose a pound. It's very depressing.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yes, well, losing weight can be a lifelong struggle. Takes a commitment. If you're ready to accept that, there are a number of things I can suggest--

speaker: Waitress
text: May I take your order, please?

speaker: Frasier
text: Um, Don, what was that?

speaker: Don
text: Oh, nothing. It was the radio. Oh, go ahead. You, you were talking.

speaker: Frasier
text: Don, where are you?

speaker: Don
text: I'm just driving around.

speaker: Waitress
text: Please, speak into the clown's mouth.

speaker: Frasier
text: Don...

speaker: Don
text: Sorry, Dr. Crane. Oh, I'm gonna lose you. I'm going into a tunnel. Goodbye.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yes, and the light at the end of that tunnel is a heat lamp over a large order of fries.

speaker: Frasier
text: We'll be right back after the news.

speaker: Roz
text: Hey, Frasier, I gotta run up to Payroll. - Be back in five. - Okay.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, hi, Father Mike.

speaker: Mike
text: - Oh, hello, Frasier. Fine. - How're you doing? Say, I just heard a rumor that somebody around here is being let go. Do you know anything about that? Because, to tell you the truth, I'm afraid it might be me.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, Father, you should know better than to put any stock in idle office gossip.

speaker: Mike
text: I know, I know, but it's hard not to. My numbers have been down lately. They keep changing my time slot. I'm really bummed.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, listen, Father, I don't like to engage in gossip, but you have nothing to worry about.

speaker: Mike
text: Yes? Why?

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, someone is being let go. But it's not you. It's Bulldog.

speaker: Mike
text: - Bulldog! Oh, what a shame. - Yes. Has anybody spoken for his parking space?

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, I have.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yes.

speaker: Bulldog
text: So I'm a goner, huh?

speaker: Frasier
text: Bulldog! How long have you been...?

speaker: Bulldog
text: Long enough to know I'm the one who's out. I knew it! I knew it! I knew it! Oh, damn it!

speaker: Bulldog
text: Now I know why Ned Miller wants to see me after work. It's to can my butt. Why would he be willing to miss happy hour at El Paquito's? The man is a total boozer!

speaker: Frasier
text: Now, now. This is just a rumor. You know how out of the loop I am.

speaker: Bulldog
text: And after all I've done for this station, this is how they repay me! That's it! Nobody fires Bob Brisco.

speaker: Frasier
text: - I'll quit first. - Now, now, don't do anything rash. Now listen, I suggest you just try to vent your anger first.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, there, way to go. - Now, on your way. - You're damn right.

speaker: Bulldog
text: - Hey, Bulldog. - No time to talk, slim. I'm off to war.

speaker: Bulldog
text: Wait for me.

speaker: Roz
text: What was that?

speaker: Frasier
text: - Bulldog's quitting. - Why? Well, because Ned Miller is firing him.

speaker: Roz
text: - Who told you that? - You did. That was just a rumor. You didn't tell him that, did you?

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, I didn't mean to. He overheard me.

speaker: Roz
text: Oh, God!

speaker: Frasier
text: What? I mean, come on, you guys were so positive. The expense account thing, meeting with management at 5.

speaker: Roz
text: That meeting was to discuss taking his show national. Don't you know anything that goes on around here?

speaker: Frasier
text: Apparently not!

speaker: Roz
text: Don't stand there. Call his secretary. She'll stop him before he gets in.

speaker: Frasier
text: I don't believe this! This is incredible. Yes, hello, hello, Arlene, Arlene. Yes, listen, Bob Brisco's about to jump into the office and... Oh, he did. Oh.

speaker: Frasier
text: God, he's already burst into the office with Miller. - Oh, God, this is a disaster. - Maybe not.

speaker: Roz
text: Maybe before Bulldog starts anything, Miller will tell him what the meeting was really about.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, I suppose you're right. Yeah, they may be having a good laugh about this right now.

speaker: unknown
text: Yeah.

speaker: Roz
text: Grab that mike. We're after the news in one minute.

speaker: Bulldog
text: I did it! I scorched him! You should've seen the look on his face. I told him about the time his wife came on to me at the Christmas party. I said there wasn't enough liquor in the world to make me sleep with that porker.

speaker: Frasier
text: - You said that? - Yeah! Yeah! Yeah!

speaker: Bulldog
text: He even took a swing at me. I gave him a little okey-dokey. He hit air!

speaker: Frasier
text: My God! The man tried to strike you! Listen--

speaker: Bulldog
text: Hey. Hey! No sudden moves, doc. I'm still too pumped. I feel like popping someone.

speaker: Frasier
text: My God, my God, this is unbelievable. A man has quit his job just because of a rumor that you spread!

speaker: Roz
text: Me? The point of gossip is to talk behind the persons back, not in front of him. I didn't realize you were unclear on this concept!

speaker: Frasier
text: I'm a bad, bad man.

speaker: Roz
text: Well, Frasier, you have got to do something. You've gotta call Ned Miller and get this whole thing cleared up.

speaker: Frasier
text: "Call Ned Miller. Clear this thing up." The man is totally unstable. He tried to take a swing at me the day he hired me.

speaker: Dave
text: Oh, I just heard a hot rumor. Bulldog quit! - No kidding. - But keep it under your hat. Very hush, hush.

speaker: Martin
text: Oh, Niles, what brings you here?

speaker: Niles
text: Well, I was hoping Daphne could take a look at this plant.

speaker: Niles
text: I bought it for Maris, but it unaccountably turned against her.

speaker: Niles
text: I thought Daphne was the perfect person to nurse it back to health with her soft, sensual hands and her loving manner. Is she here?

speaker: Martin
text: No, she stepped out. I don't know when she'll be back.

speaker: Niles
text: - Well, I'm off. - Well, hey, you can stay.

speaker: Martin
text: I haven't seen you for a while. We can visit.

speaker: unknown
text: Uh--

speaker: Niles
text: Well, yes, we could, couldn't we?

speaker: Niles
text: - So, how are you? - Fine.

speaker: Martin
text: - You? - Fine.

speaker: Niles
text: She's fine.

speaker: Martin
text: Pickle?

speaker: Niles
text: No, thanks.

speaker: Martin
text: Look, Niles, if you just came to see Daphne, you don't have to stay.

speaker: Niles
text: Dad, I can't believe you would say that to your own son. I am deeply insulted. Here I wanted to have some time with you, but now I'm so upset I'll have to leave.

speaker: Daphne
text: Oh, hello, Dr. Crane. Staying for dinner?

speaker: Niles
text: Yes, love to. Daphne, I had the fervent hope that you could coax this back to life. It's one of Maris' favorites.

speaker: Daphne
text: My goodness, what did she do to it?

speaker: Niles
text: Nothing. Just loved it.

speaker: Frasier
text: God, do you believe this weather?

speaker: Martin
text: I'm glad you're home. What happened to Bulldog?

speaker: Frasier
text: Who told you?

speaker: Martin
text: Nobody told me anything. I tuned into the Gonzo Sports Show today like I always do, and they had Father Mike filling in. I hate that. All it was, was Notre Dame, Notre Dame, Notre Dame.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yes, well, Bulldog tendered his resignation.

speaker: Martin
text: Oh, no! Why would he do that? He's the top sports guy in town.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yeah, you know, things just go funny sometimes. It's a tough business, this radio game, you know?

speaker: Daphne
text: Dr. Crane, I'm picking up something from you. You're shrouded in an aura of guilt.

speaker: Frasier
text: Maybe I am.

speaker: Niles
text: Daphne, that's fantastic. Do me. Do me.

speaker: Daphne
text: No, I'm on to something here. You actually think you're responsible for Bulldog losing his job.

speaker: Frasier
text: - Frasier? - All right, all right. There was a rumor going around the station that Bulldog was gonna get sacked, I was repeating it to someone and he overheard me and flew off the handle and went up and quit his job. In the end, it turned out that the rumor wasn't true. Of course, you already knew that, didn't you?

speaker: Niles
text: Oh, excuse me.

speaker: Niles
text: Hello. Maris. Maris, what's wrong? Oh, pumpkin, it's all right. No, no, everything's going to be... Oh, dear. I'm sorry, I have to go. Maris is despondent. They've kicked her out of the cast of Cats.

speaker: Daphne
text: Why?

speaker: Niles
text: She couldn't remember the words to "Memory."

speaker: Martin
text: Now, listen here, if you're responsible for Bulldog losing his job, you gotta make this right. Go to that station to talk to the boss and get him his job back.

speaker: Frasier
text: That's easier said than done. Ned Miller's the most intimidating, heartless, mean-spirited man I've ever met.

speaker: Daphne
text: And he cheats on his wife.

speaker: Daphne
text: My goodness, I'm on today. Ooh.

speaker: Martin
text: So you sold Bulldog down the river just because you don't have the guts to go and face this guy?

speaker: Frasier
text: This might be the best thing that ever happened to him. He's always talking about how he should be in a larger market like Los Angeles or New York. Eddie, just scoot. Scat!

speaker: unknown
text: Stay.

speaker: Frasier
text: - Bulldog. - Hi, doc. What are you doing just standing there?

speaker: Bulldog
text: I don't know. I was trying to decide whether or not I should bother you. See, my life is kind of over, but you got company, so I'll go.

speaker: Frasier
text: No, no, no, come in, come in. This is just family. This is my dad and Daphne Moon.

speaker: Martin
text: - Hello. - Hey, Bulldog! You're soaking wet.

speaker: Bulldog
text: Yeah, I've been wandering around the streets for the last few hours.

speaker: Martin
text: I heard what happened.

speaker: Bulldog
text: You haven't heard the half of it. My girlfriend threw me out. She said the only reason she was with me was because I was on the radio. Can you believe that? Eight years we've been together. I loved that woman. Even when I was tomcatting around, I loved that woman.

speaker: Bulldog
text: God, that job was my life, and now I've been blackballed in this business, and all because of my stupid temper. What is this, anyway?

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, that, that's an exceedingly rare fertility symbol from a small nomadic tribe in Ghana.

speaker: Bulldog
text: I guess when they were passing out equipment, this guy was in the back of the line. Anyway, I might as well face it, I'm just a loser. I'm a zero, a nothing, a has-been.

speaker: Martin
text: Pickle?

speaker: Daphne
text: Now I'm not familiar with your work myself, but Mr. Crane here often puts off his nightly bath just so he can hear your show.

speaker: Martin
text: Oh, yeah, you're the greatest, Bulldog. If you weren't on the radio, I wouldn't have a radio.

speaker: Bulldog
text: That's a nice thing to say. Now I know why your son is such a great guy.

speaker: Bulldog
text: Hey, uh, I've bothered you people enough. I better go. The good rooms at the Y fill up early.

speaker: Frasier
text: Wait, Bulldog, I can't let you leave like this.

speaker: Frasier
text: Here's a 20.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, all right, why don't you spend the night and you can take the couch.

speaker: Bulldog
text: - Wow. You'd do that for me? - Well, sure.

speaker: Frasier
text: What's the point of having a suede couch unless you have people crashing on it?

speaker: Bulldog
text: Thanks, doc. Hey, I hope it's okay, but I could really use a hot shower.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, sure, sure.

speaker: Daphne
text: Down the hall. Second door on the left. Towels are in the cabinet.

speaker: Frasier
text: Now you two just leave me alone. This is not my fault. Look, I am not responsible for Bulldog going up there and popping off to the boss. You can stare at me until you're blue in the face. I am not gonna go see Ned Miller.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, all right!

speaker: Frasier
text: I'll go down to that station. I will talk to the monster on the sixth floor and futilely attempt to get a man back his job that I don't even care for, and in the process I will probably end up spitting out my teeth like Chiclets.

speaker: Frasier
text: Is there anything else I can do for you?

speaker: Daphne
text: Oh, if you're going by the market, we're low on dog food.

speaker: Miller
text: What? What?

speaker: Miller
text: - Mr. Miller... - Oh, it's you, Crane.

speaker: Frasier
text: - Arlene wasn't at her desk. - No, I had to let her go.

speaker: Miller
text: A lot of stuff she's been doing lately has been ticking me off.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, if this is a bad time...

speaker: Miller
text: No, it's a perfect time. I need you to hold this. Come on. Now.

speaker: unknown
text: Jeez. Come on.

speaker: Frasier
text: Okay. How's this?

speaker: Miller
text: I'd love to tell you, but your big head's in the way.

speaker: Miller
text: Oh, put it down.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, my Lord, what happened here?

speaker: Miller
text: Oh, that psycho Bulldog and I got into it this afternoon. He threw my Golden Mic at me.

speaker: Frasier
text: He did that with your little trophy?

speaker: Miller
text: No, he just chipped the paint with the trophy. I did that with his head.

speaker: Frasier
text: - Uh, that's sort of why I'm here. - Drink? No, no, thank you, Mr. Miller. I know that Bulldog was up here, and he said some things to you.

speaker: Miller
text: I'll say he said some things. You wanna hear them? I tape everything in this office.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, anyway, a lot of what he said was my fault, you see. Well, you see, I heard a rumor that management was thinking about lightening the load a bit. Well, I heard that it was Bulldog that was gonna get sacked. And I... I was repeating a rumor to someone, and Bulldog heard me. And that's why he came up here and started telling you--

speaker: Miller
text: That I'm a drunk. That I'm incompetent at my job. That my wife is a big, fat slut.

speaker: Frasier
text: That is indefensible. Your wife is not overweight!

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, uh... Well, anyway, my point is that, uh...

speaker: Frasier
text: I'd like you to consider giving Bulldog his job back. And whatever the consequences to me, I'm willing to accept it.

speaker: Miller
text: Look, I won't kid you. Bulldog meant big numbers to us in drive time. We need him back. I'll tell you what. You get him to apologize to me. Oh, hell, why don't I just say it? If he'll kiss my ass, maybe we can work something out.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, sir, I'm sure that'll make him so happy. Um-- Well, I'll just get out of your hair.

speaker: Miller
text: Actually, Crane, that rumor about someone being let go... - it's, uh, true. - What? Now that you've so nobly gotten Bulldog his job back, the station still needs to make some cutbacks in those high-priced salaries.

speaker: Frasier
text: God, not Father Mike! Oh, no.

speaker: Miller
text: No, it's not Father Mike.

speaker: Frasier
text: Chopper Dave?

speaker: Frasier
text: Ray the Green Grocer?

speaker: Frasier
text: Bonnie "The Auto Lady" Weems?

speaker: Miller
text: Look, Crane, you're new to the radio game. I've been around a long time. People get fired, but they always get back on their feet. So I bet I could get you that drink now.

speaker: Frasier
text: Yes, I bet you could.

speaker: Miller
text: Help yourself. Ned Miller! Yo, Jack! No, what's wrong? Come on, tell me now. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Yeah, I see. No, no, no, I... I got it.

speaker: Miller
text: Thanks, Jack.

speaker: Miller
text: Excuse me.

speaker: Miller
text: - Bad news? - Oh, you could say that. I've just been fired. They decided the best way to cut the budget was to get rid of my high salary.

speaker: Frasier
text: Oh, Ned, I... I'm so sorry.

speaker: Frasier
text: Then I guess this means that my job is still safe then?

speaker: Miller
text: Yeah, I guess so.

speaker: Frasier
text: Well, you know, Ned...

speaker: Frasier
text: I haven't been in the radio game that long...

speaker: Frasier
text: but I've been around long enough to know that people get fired. And when they do, they always seem to land on their feet. Now, I've known quite a few people and counseled them who have suffered similar setbacks, but in time you will embrace this. Learn to think of it as, oh, a new chapter. You know, in theatrical circles, they always say, "Every exit is but an entrance to somewhere else."

speaker: Miller
text: God, I wish I had fired you when I had the chance.
